A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 24 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments and analyses of ventilation rates and duration in eICU and MIMIC-IV, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical analyses and adds estimator comparisons, demographic summaries, and group-imbalance experiments.

M1.justification: The VDE estimand, nuisance parameters, cross-fitted doubly robust estimator, and self-normalization procedure remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and newly evaluated comparators do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds controlled semi-synthetic population scenarios with subgroup proportions of 0.1, 0.2, 0.33, and 0.5. The clinical datasets, ventilation outcomes, and continuous and binary synthetic data families remain the same.

E2.justification: Appendix I/Table 4 adds explicit comparisons against the X-learner, a single-mediator doubly robust estimator, and nested regression across four existing settings. Previously, empirical estimator comparisons primarily concerned canonical versus self-normalized estimation. V2 acknowledges that some added comparators target different effects.

E3.justification: V2 adds fixed-32,000-sample VDE-error comparisons and a protocol that thresholds predicted X values to control subgroup prevalence. The reported eICU cohort changes from 37,250 to 37,222 admissions. Existing fold counts, propensity clipping, and selected hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix J/Figure 14 newly tests sensitivity to group imbalance in both semi-synthetic cohorts. Appendix C/Figure 8 adds age and sex distributions by race. Existing nuisance-parameter, binary-synthetic, and conditional-VDE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports means and standard errors over 100 bootstraps. Existing experiments retain 100 or 500 bootstraps and 95% confidence intervals. Changed interval widths do not establish an increase in repetitions or a revised uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Several central clinical estimates change: Figure 5 reports eICU VDE rates of -0.34 versus -0.21 percentage points and durations of 0.8 versus 2.3 hours; its duration NIE* changes from -2.3 to 0.4 hours. MIMIC-IV duration VDE remains 7.4 hours, but its reported CI changes from [7.2, 7.7] to [6.9, 7.9]. Conditional findings in Figure 6 also change, and Table 4/Figure 14 add comparative and robustness results. These are revised estimates, not demonstrated performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly asserts that the theoretical results extend analogously to the self-normalized estimator. This modestly extends the stated theoretical scope, although the formal statements and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged and no separate self-normalization proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, primary contributions, and concluding claims retain the same causal pipeline, estimator contributions, and clinical conclusions: small ventilation-rate effects and larger, dataset-dependent duration effects. Additional validation does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds clinical explanations involving clinicians' use of additional information and potentially uncaptured causal pathways. It explicitly discusses practical graph-misspecification limitations and explains why V includes physiological oxygen measurements alongside discrepancy. Existing temporality and sparse-measurement limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies the estimator-count search grid {20, 50, 100, 200}, while Table 3's selected configurations remain identical. V2 also clarifies adult-only analysis and documents the new experiments. Hardware, runtime statements, dataset versions, and stated code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lederer et al. on causal-confounding reporting and Matos et al. on BOLD, including attribution in Figure 1. It also explains its relationship to single-mediator methods and Miles et al. more explicitly. Most bibliography changes are metadata or formatting updates.

P1.justification: V2 polishes the introduction and related-work prose, standardizes terminology toward 'canonical' estimation, and expands Conclusions into Discussion. Author affiliations, conference information, and acknowledgements change, but the main narrative sequence and proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the demographic Figure 8, imbalance Figure 14, and comparison Table 4. Existing displays are relocated or renumbered, captions are refined, and Figure 6's color scales change. The overall layout and principal graphical formats remain similar.

improvement.justification: The new imbalance experiment makes an important applicability concern directly assessable, while fuller tuning documentation and more explicit clinical and causal caveats improve transparency. These gains are limited: the added comparison includes methods targeting different effects, and Appendix I's claim of consistently lowest error is not supported by every Table 4 column. The revision improves assessment of robustness and applicability without establishing a substantially stronger overall paper.
